citations.quote:
Use a smooth, oriented and time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N,o)$
of signature $(-,+,+,+)$, as in [[def-tgr-framework-units]]. The manifold
orientation is independent of the time orientation. On an open set $U\subseteq
M$, let $F$ be a smooth real two-form and use the SI constants and
length-coordinate convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. This adoption is
parameterized by any complete explicitly supplied named smooth classical
matter-model instance
$$\mathcal M=(\mathcal C_m,\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m)$$
of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]]. The model data are inputs, not
unspecified functions to be inferred from the field equation. They specify
the actual matter-field bundles and smooth configuration fields $\Psi$ in
$\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ on $U$, the exact equations and constraints
$\mathcal E_m[g,F;\Psi]=0$, all constitutive functions and parameters, and
the explicit current and symmetric-stress maps $\mathsf J_m$ and
$\mathsf T_m$. Any further domain, boundary or initial-data hypotheses of
that selected model are retained. A specialization must give these actual
equations and maps together with the model's name; providing only the symbols
$\mathcal E_m,\mathsf J_m,\mathsf T_m$ or arbitrary smooth $j,T^m$ is not
such a specification.

For the supplied model, take an admitted smooth configuration
$\Psi\in\mathcal C_m[g,F]$ satisfying all of its equations and constraints,
and set
$$j:=\mathsf J_m[g,F;\Psi],\qquad T^m:=\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi].$$
Thus $j$ is a smooth vector field and $T^m$ is a smooth symmetric covariant
two-tensor on the same domain. The postulate and the restricted area deduction
are uniform in these fully specified model data; they do not select one
constitutive law or restrict the range to source-free matter or dust. The
named zero-matter instance, when selected, is precisely $\mathcal M_0$ of
the equation-based supplier. No matter action or circle-representation
hypothesis is required for this model input.

Define
$$T_{ab}:=T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab},\qquad T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}:=\frac1{\mu_0}\left(F_{ac}F_b{}^c-\frac14g_{ab}F_{cd}F^{cd}\right),$$
where raised indices use $g^{-1}$ and $\mu_0>0$. Define
$G_{ab}:=\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}-\tfrac12 Rg_{ab}$ with the curvature
convention of [[def-emg-lorentzian-forms]]. Adopt the smooth Maxwell equations
$dF=0$ and $\nabla_aF^{ab}=-\mu_0j^b$, together with the equation-based
gravitational field law of [[post-emg-einstein-maxwell-equations]] on $U$:
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\frac{8\pi G_N}{c^4}T_{ab},$$
with constant $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $G_N>0$, and $c>0$.

For a specified smooth embedded null hypersurface $H\subset U$ and a smooth
nowhere-zero future-directed null generator field $k$ along $H$, adopt the
null energy condition on this generator:
$$T_{ab}k^ak^b\ge0\qquad\text{at every point of }H.$$
Here $H$, $k$, and the screen variables are defined by
[[def-tgr-horizon-screen-family]]; the displayed inequality is a physical
restriction on the selected classical stress and congruence. It is not a
consequence of the field equation and is not asserted for every quantum state.
For the restricted area result on this page, the chosen generator must also
have the smooth future flow and persistent compact spacelike cuts stated in
[[thm-tgr-smooth-null-area]]. This adoption neither constructs such a flow or
horizon nor asserts that every event horizon has those regularity and
completeness properties. No matter action, singular source, observational
claim, or thermodynamic entropy is included.

For constant cosmological parameter $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4$, adopt the additional equation-based gravitational field law $$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa_E\left(T^{\mathrm{EM}}_{ab}+T^m_{ab}\right).$$
Use the unique torsion-free metric-compatible connection $\nabla^g$ and the curvature convention of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] and [[thm-gr-curvature-tensoriality-and-coordinate-formula]].
A **smooth affine null generator field** on $H$ is a smooth vector field $k$ along $H$ such that $k_p$ is a nonzero future-directed section of $L_p$ and $\nabla_k k=0$ along $H$.
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following statement.

Then $\theta\ge0$ everywhere on every $S_\lambda$. Let $q_\lambda:=\Phi_\lambda^*g$ be the induced Riemannian metric on $S_0$, let $\mu_{q_\lambda}$ be its Riemannian volume density, and define $$A(\lambda):=\int_{S_0}\mu_{q_\lambda}=\int_{S_\lambda}\mu_{g|_{S_\lambda}},$$ where the second equality is the density change-of-variables formula for the embedding $\Phi_\lambda$. Then for every $\lambda>\lambda_0$, $$A'(\lambda)=\int_{S_0}\theta(\Phi(\lambda,x))\,\mu_{q_\lambda}(x)=\int_{S_\lambda}\theta\,dA\ge0,$$ and $A(\lambda_2)\ge A(\lambda_1)$ whenever $\lambda_2\ge\lambda_1\ge\lambda_0$.

derivations.claim:
For the supplied model and admitted configuration in [F1] and [A1], use
$T=T^{\mathrm{EM}}+\mathsf T_m[g,F;\Psi]$ from that same configuration.
Set $\kappa_E:=8\pi G_N/c^4>0$ and contract its adopted field equation
from [F1]–[F2] with $k^ak^b$. Since $k$ is null,
$g_{ab}k^ak^b=0$, so both the cosmological term and the scalar-curvature
term in $G_{ab}k^ak^b$ vanish. The resulting identity is
$\operatorname{Ric}_{ab}k^ak^b=\kappa_E T_{ab}k^ak^b\ge0$ by [A1]. The
curvature convention in [F3] identifies this Ricci contraction with the one
in [F6]; hence the required null-convergence hypothesis holds along the full
flow.

The geometric assumptions [F4], [A2], and [A3] match the screen,
affine-flow, persistent-cut, and choice hypotheses of [F6]. Applying that
mathematical theorem gives $\theta\ge0$ and the stated area derivative
identity; its area density is positive, so $A_H'(\lambda)\ge0$ for
$\lambda>\lambda_0$. Its endpoint continuity and monotonicity conclusion
give $A_H(\lambda_2)\ge A_H(\lambda_1)$ for every
$\lambda_2\ge\lambda_1\ge\lambda_0$. This is a model deduction under the
adopted postulates, not an inference from observation.

derivations.claim:
The parameter map [F1], [F8], under the inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$
convention [F7], sends every stated SI triple to a point
$(m,a,q)\in\mathcal P$ and makes the full domain strict subextremal. When
$a^2+q^2>0$, [L1] supplies the selected outer horizon, its constant
cross-section data, and the stated time and gauge normalizations. At the
remaining point $a=q=0$, [F6] supplies the exact Schwarzschild horizon data;
[F3]–[F4] keep this specialization within the selected physical solution
family and its smooth ingoing model. Hence the geometric quantities used in
[F5] coincide with the selected model's horizon quantities throughout the
stated physical domain.

Write $j:=ma$. From [F1], [F8], $$E_{\rm par}=\frac{c^4}{G_N}m,\qquad j=\frac{G_N}{c^3}J,\qquad q=\sqrt{\frac{G_N}{4\pi\varepsilon_0c^4}}\,Q_e.$$ 
The horizon formulas give $\Omega_{\rm SI}=c\Omega_{\rm KN}$ and
$\kappa_{\rm acc}=c^2\kappa_{\rm KN}$. For the voltage,
$$\frac c\alpha=c\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c^4}{4\pi G_N}}=\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}},$$
where the last equality uses $\varepsilon_0\mu_0c^2=1$ from [F8]. Thus
$\Phi_{\rm SI}=(c^2/\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N})\Phi_{\rm KN}$,
and the area $A_H$ is the same $A$ as in [F5].

Multiply the first identity in [F5] by $c^4/G_N$. The $dm$ term
becomes $dE_{\rm par}$; the area term becomes
$\kappa_{\rm acc}c^2dA_H/(8\pi G_N)$; and the angular term becomes
$\Omega_{\rm SI}dJ$ by [F1] and step 1.2. The charge term becomes
$$\frac{c^4}{G_N}\Phi_{\rm KN}\,dq=\frac{c^2}{\sqrt{4\pi\varepsilon_0G_N}}\Phi_{\rm KN}\,dQ_e=\Phi_{\rm SI}\,dQ_e,$$
using fixed constants and step 1.2. This proves the physical-unit family
differential identity.

Multiply the Smarr identity in [F5] by $c^4/G_N$. Applying the same
constant conversions from step 1.2 sends its four terms respectively to
$E_{\rm par}$, $\kappa_{\rm acc}c^2A_H/(4\pi G_N)$,
$2\Omega_{\rm SI}J$, and $\Phi_{\rm SI}Q_e$. This proves the displayed
Smarr identity on the same strict domain. These are identities between
stationary family parameters, not a time-dependent process or an ADM/Komar
energy theorem.

The inherited $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ premise [F2] is retained; the finite
parameter calculation below makes no stronger choice. Set
$m:=G_Nm_*/c^2$. By [F1], the geometric horizon radius is
$2m$, so $A_H=16\pi m^2=16\pi G_N^2m_*^2/c^4$ and

This verifies the stated family differential identity exactly.
